title: Capstone Walkthrough: Performance Audit
objective: After this lesson you will be able to run a full performance audit — inventory slow queries, EXPLAIN each, rank by impact (frequency × cost), apply rewrites and indexes in priority order, verify every arrow, and deliver findings plus guardrails — ready for the final assessment and your own audit project.
why: Courses 1–9 taught moves; audits are the job. A performance audit is bounded, evidence-driven, and shippable: N queries in, measured wins plus prevention rules out. This walkthrough performs a miniature audit on the catalog's own dashboard queries — the exact rehearsal your capstone project scales up.

blocks.text: The audit brief and its budget

Brief: *'Three dashboard queries timeout under load; find the wins worth shipping this week.'* Budget: four hours, no schema redesigns (indexes and rewrites only), every claim measured. Scoping is the first skill: audits without budgets become rewrites of everything; budgets force impact-ranked priorities — frequency × per-run cost, biggest product first.

Per-course totals via correlated scalar, ordered by the computed count, page 30 via OFFSET. Plan: per-row probes (N executions), TEMP B-TREE over all courses, linear skip of 580 rows. Fix sequence: flatten to grouped derived table (Ch.3), keyset on (total, id) (Ch.3), composite on the FK iff probes still scan (Ch.2). Expected: the case-study curve — seconds to tenths.

blocks.code:
-- Audit exhibit A: the shape (real SQLite/PostgreSQL)
-- BEFORE: SELECT c.title,
--   (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM enrollments e WHERE e.course_id = c.id) AS total
-- FROM courses c ORDER BY total DESC LIMIT 20 OFFSET 580;
-- AFTER: WITH per_course AS (
--   SELECT course_id, COUNT(*) AS total FROM enrollments GROUP BY course_id)
-- SELECT c.title, COALESCE(p.total, 0) AS total
-- FROM courses c LEFT JOIN per_course p ON p.course_id = c.id
-- WHERE (COALESCE(p.total, 0), c.id) < (?, ?)
-- ORDER BY total DESC, c.id DESC LIMIT 20;
blocks.caption: Exhibit A: flatten + keyset — the case-study moves, compressed

blocks.text: Topic-or-role search with leading wildcards on both sides: unindexable twice over. Fix in two horizons: this week, sargabilize (exact/prefix match) and split OR into UNION ALL with disjoint guards (Ch.3); documented follow-up, trigram/full-text search for genuine substring needs (honest scoping — the audit says what it defers, with the reason).

Per-role average hours computed *after* joining enrollments: fanout weights multi-enrolled developers multiply (Ch.5/Intermediate). Fix: aggregate developers alone first (CTE), join enrollments only where needed — or recognize the metric never needed the join at all. Impact-ranked third (correctness inflected as performance: wrong fast is still wrong).

blocks.caption: Exhibit B: the join was the bug — removal beats optimization

blocks.text: Rank by impact: suspect 1 (every load, seconds) → suspect 3 (wrong numbers, trust) → suspect 2 (occasional search). Deliverable structure: per-suspect baseline plan + timing, change, re-plan + timing, guardrail (keyset contract, sargability rule, review-checklist entry from Ch.9). Plus the deferred list with reasons — audits earn trust by scoping visibly.

blocks.query: SELECT role, AVG(hours_studied) AS avg_hours, COUNT(*) AS devs FROM developers GROUP BY role ORDER BY avg_hours DESC;
blocks.note: Run this correct-by-construction rollup in the sandbox — no join, no fanout possible. Contrast it mentally with the joined version: same intent, inflated numbers. Deleting joins is an optimization.

items: Scope audits: bounded time, rewrites+indexes only, impact-ranked (frequency × cost)
Apply the course in order: EXPLAIN (1), rewrite shapes (3), index proof (2), verify arrows
Correctness defects (fanout) outrank speed defects — wrong fast is still wrong
Deliver baselines, changes, verifications, guardrails — plus an explicit deferred list

exercise.prompt: Mini-audit rehearsal on the stalled-learners report: (a) sandbox the flat shape and record rows/timing feel; (b) write the three-suspect treatment for real SQLite/PostgreSQL — baseline EXPLAIN shape, one rewrite, one index decision with justification; (c) draft the guardrail line that prevents regression (which Ch.9 checklist entry, enforced how?).
hints: Sandbox flat: per-developer completions via GROUP BY + HAVING SUM(completed) = 0 — the preservation baseline every rewrite must match row-for-row.
Treatment: EXPLAIN the grouped join (probes? sorts?), flatten anything correlated (none here — note its absence as a finding), composite on (developer_id) iff probes scan, keyset if paginated.
Guardrail example: 'Paginated reports use keyset bookmarks — enforced by Ch.9 review checklist item, verified by EXPLAIN showing no OFFSET skip in CI-visible slow-query log.'
exercise.solution:
-- (a) sandbox baseline (flat — run here; record counts)
-- per-developer completions + stalled filter (see lesson shapes)
-- (b) treatment: EXPLAIN → probes SEARCH? sort needed? → minimal index → re-verify
-- (c) guardrail: keyset-only pagination + sargability review items on this report's file.
exercise.why: The rehearsal scales down the audit loop to one report: baseline, treatment, guardrail. Performing it small is what makes the full capstone tractable — audits are fractal.
exercise.code:
-- Sandbox baseline (flat — run here)
SELECT d.name, COUNT(*) AS started, SUM(e.completed) AS done
FROM developers d JOIN enrollments e ON e.developer_id = d.id
GROUP BY d.id HAVING SUM(e.completed) = 0;

-- Treatment + guardrail (real SQLite / PostgreSQL — see solution).

quiz.q: Three slow queries, four hours, no schema redesigns. How do you order the work?
options: Impact-ranked: frequency × per-run cost, biggest product first — within a fixed scope
quiz.explain: Audits are budgeted: impact ranking spends hours where users feel them. Scope (rewrites+indexes only) prevents redesign sprawl; the deferred list preserves honesty.

quiz.q: A rollup is both slow AND inflated after a join. Which do you fix first?
options: Correctness (fanout) — wrong fast is still wrong; then the speed
quiz.explain: Inflated numbers erode trust that speed can't restore. Remove/isolate the fanout first (often deleting the join), then optimize the correct shape.

quiz.q: Your fix works but the ticket reappears in three months with the old shape back. What was missing?
options: Guardrails: documented contracts (keyset rule, checklist entries) that prevent regression — performance without prevention rots
quiz.explain: Wins without contracts decay as new code repeats old shapes. The deliverable includes prevention: rules, checklist items, and the deferred list with reasons.

quiz.q: When is 'defer to trigram/FTS later' the right audit call on substring search?
options: When the budget covers sargabilize+split wins now, and genuine substring needs exceed LIKE's capability — scoped openly with reasons, not silently dropped
quiz.explain: Audits earn trust by visible scoping: ship this week's wins, name next quarter's project with its justification. Deferred-with-reasons beats silent omission and gold-plating alike.

summary: Audit = scope, baseline, impact-rank, rewrite-then-index per suspect, verify every arrow, deliver findings + guardrails + deferred list. The capstone scales this loop to your own audit — course complete, assessment next.
